content.thinking:
I'm piecing together the timeline: the flag was off before 01:02 with normal account page rendering and pre-existing disconnect errors, then at 01:02 an admin toggled it on, logs show mixed on/off evaluations, and a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 started appearing right at that moment.

Interestingly, when the flag was switched off at 01:08:14, logs still show it evaluating as "on" through 01:10 — so the mitigation attempt never actually propagated, which is why it was refuted rather than the flag itself being ruled out as the cause. Tracing the chain: account page failures stem from the ZeroDivisionError, which stems from the newly enabled monthly-spend-feature code path, which per spec divides by the count of purchases this month — failing for shoppers with zero purchases.

I'm also ruling out deploys as a cause since no production changes besides the flag toggle appeared in the deploy history, and rollout had already converged across replicas; the pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors ended right at onset, making them baseline noise rather than a candidate cause.

The refutation of the flag fix is real — the logs show the flag still evaluating "on" in the provider through 01:10 despite the switch-off, which conflicts with expectations but matches the record. This points to a contributing factor: the flag system failed to propagate the off-switch promptly, meaning the revert action couldn't stop the incident as soon as it should have.

Also worth noting nobody was paged — that's a contributing factor of its own, since no on-call paging was linked to this alert rule, and a person being brought in might have caught the flag issue sooner. I'm leaning toward classifying it as a contributing factor rather than went_wrong, since it's a pre-existing condition.

I'm also considering test coverage gaps as another contributing factor — the monthly path with no purchases wasn't covered by existing tests, based on F1's note that the new test cases would fail against current code.

Two more candidates: the flag rollout wasn't staged (it went from partial to fully on almost instantly, with no canary or gradual percentage), and the flag provider's off-switch apparently didn't take effect in the service after the fix attempt. I want to propose remediation items for both — progressive rollout with error-rate guards, and verifying the off-switch actually propagates.

Also nobody got paged despite the HighErrorRate alert, so that needs to be linked to on-call paging. I'm also considering whether to add an action item to keep the monthly-spend-feature flag off until the real fix is merged, given it's currently back on despite the underlying issue.

I should stay cautious about claiming the service recovered — with the flag back on and the division fault still present, shoppers with no purchases this month would likely keep seeing failed account pages, and turning the flag off at the provider hadn't actually been shown to stop the service from evaluating it as on.

Building the causal chain: account page requests started failing broadly, with error rates spiking from baseline to a peak, citing the relevant logs and series data. The root cause traces to a ZeroDivisionError thrown at spend_summary.py line 47, first logged around 01:02.

Tracing further back, an admin enabled the monthly-spend feature flag, which the service began evaluating as "on" for a growing share of evaluations—before this it was off and pages rendered fine. I'm ruling out deploys as a cause since none occurred in this window.

Since there's no earlier change on record, that's confirmed and not worth further comment. The real mechanism is in F1: the function divides this month's total by this-month purchase count, which is zero for returning shoppers who haven't bought yet this month — flipping the flag routed those shoppers through this broken path, so that's where the explanation stops. Timeline-wise, the flag reverted at T18, Argus linked the onset to the flag change forming C1 right after the alert, and the revert followed shortly after that, with Code-Fix drafting a PR in response.

The second investigation also caught that logs still showed the flag evaluating as on even after the supposed switch-off, which is the C2 finding backed by Gce95 — that held up as a legitimate catch. Where things went wrong is that Mitigation judged the revert refuted and flipped the flag back on without noticing the logs proved the revert had never actually taken effect, meaning it tested a flag state that wasn't really reverted; it also checked the service only about a second after the revert, which seems far too soon to draw a real conclusion.

I'm noting that Argus moved to FIXING claiming no explanation was left to pursue, even though C2 clearly pointed at the flag-evaluation issue in the flag system itself — that thread was left unexplored. As for lucky breaks, shoppers who'd made purchases this month were unaffected per F1, which feels more like a narrow scope of the bug than real luck, so I'm skipping that.

For assumptions, I'm noting the cause mechanism comes from F1, the account-page error rate (Gbac1) is being treated as representative of the service-wide alert rate, the flag-still-on-after-switchoff conclusion comes from log lines rather than the flag system directly, and the customer loss figure is explicitly a lower bound per the document.

Now listing contributing factors: missing test coverage for the monthly-spend-summary edge case (addressed by AI-1), the flag being switched on for all shoppers simultaneously with no staged rollout or automatic error-rate guard, the flag continuing to evaluate as "on" for two minutes after the provider switch-off (needs investigation), and the alert not being linked to paging so no human was brought in when the automated revert failed.

For action items: fix why io-shop kept evaluating the flag as on after it was switched off, add a divergence check between the flag provider's state and what the service actually evaluates, and have the Mitigation Agent confirm a flag revert took effect from the service's own evaluations before concluding it was refuted. I'm also thinking about a mitigation step involving switching something, though that thought trails off.

For prevention, I want to roll out flags like monthly-spend-feature progressively to a small share of shoppers first, paired with an automatic rollback tied to account-page error rate — treating these as two separate items both tied to CF-2. Finally, as a process fix, I should link HighErrorRate on io-shop directly to on-call paging.

Now I'm being careful to avoid number words in plain-language explanations — things like "one," "two," "a third," "zero" shouldn't appear even implicitly. The root cause is that enabling monthly-spend-feature makes render_spend_summary call average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides a shopper's total spend this month by their purchase count this month — and for shoppers who've bought before but not this month, that count is empty, causing the failure.

I'm checking the went_well timeline entries for timing placeholders relative to the alert, covering the Investigator's flag identification, the Mitigation Agent's toggle test, and Code-Fix's draft PR #371, making sure each cites elapsed time without describing the underlying action.

Went wrong also includes the Investigator's second pass flagging that the flag still evaluated on after switch-off, yet Argus moved to FIXING citing no explanation left rather than digging into why the switch-off failed — I want to note this carefully without overstating it as a definitive design flaw, and I'll leave out mentioning "Argus held."

action_items.item: Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off in the flag provider, and fix it.
Alert when the state the flag provider holds for a flag differs from the state io-shop logs it evaluating.
Switch monthly-spend-feature off, confirm from io-shop's own evaluation logs that it is off, and keep it off until the proposed fix is merged.
Make the Mitigation Agent confirm from the service's own evaluations that a flag revert took effect before it judges the revert refuted and puts the flag back.
Turn monthly-spend-feature on for a small share of shoppers first, before turning it on for everyone.
Add an automatic halt that turns a flag rollout back when the account page error rate climbs after the flag changes.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of failed requests rose from {errors_before} before the onset to a peak of {errors_at_worst}. The service's own logs put the account page error rate at typically {Gbac1.6}, reaching {Gbac1.5} at {Gbac1.7}.

Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error was logged throughout {G5309.3} and did not appear in the logs read from before the onset.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the change events read for the day before the onset and after it came back with flag changes only, and no deploys.
The ClientDisconnected account page failures: they were already logged before the onset, while account pages were rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Before that the service evaluated the flag as off and account pages rendered normally. At {G971b.6}, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and from then on every evaluation logged was on.

With the flag on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides this month's total by the number of this month's purchases. For shoppers who have bought before but not this month, that number is empty, so the division raises and serve_account_page fails the request.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly spending summary sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought before but not this month, because it divides by the number of their purchases this month and they have none.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that covers the monthly spend summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. By Code-Fix's reading, the test cases it adds for that case would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division fault would likely have been caught before anyone switched the flag on, so turning it on would not have broken account pages.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every evaluation almost at once. No staged rollout, and no automatic halt tied to the account page error rate, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A smaller share of shoppers would have hit the failure, or the rollout would have stopped by itself once account page errors climbed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: Switching monthly-spend-feature off in the flag provider did not change what the service evaluated: its logs went on showing the flag as on after the switch-off at {P2.1}, through {Gce95.4}.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The revert of the flag would likely have stopped the failing account pages soon after it was made, instead of being judged ineffective.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in while the failures went on, and could have taken up the flag that would not switch off once the automated revert did not help.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator named the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature as the candidate cause C1, {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
To test C1, the Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off, {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
On its second pass, the Investigator noted in C2 that the logs still showed the flag on after the switch-off, which Gce95 bears out.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request PR #371, {T36.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the flag revert REFUTED and switched monthly-spend-feature back on. The service's own logs show it never stopped evaluating the flag as on after the switch-off, so the revert was never really tested.
Argus moved to FIXING with no explanation left to try. C2 had pointed out that the flag kept evaluating on after the switch-off, but why the switch-off did not take effect was not followed up.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides account.total_this_month_cents by the length of the shopper's list of current-month purchases. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and serve_account_page fails the account page request.
input.still_at_risk: monthly-spend-feature had been put back on and the division fault was still in the code, so account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month would likely keep failing. Switching the flag off in the provider had not been seen to stop the service evaluating it as on.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
